title: Steering Fragility Under Adversarial Paraphrase: Concept Steering Fails When Feature Activation Is Bypassed

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests robustness of SAE steering as a deployment-time safety mechanism. If paraphrase bypasses steering, the mechanism provides no adversarial robustness guarantee, which is a critical finding for deployment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Identifying SAE features, applying steering, and generating paraphrase variants are all documented procedures. Measuring whether features re-route is technically feasible with standard SAE tools. Paraphrase generation can leverage existing models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tight deliverable: for a target concept, measure feature activation rate under paraphrase variants with and without steering. Single concept, single experiment, clear binary outcome per paraphrase. 30 hours is feasible if limited to one harmful concept.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
